ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.claim: The prophet narratives share a refrain of God's peace and mercy, support for the messenger's mission, and reward for good deeds; this refrain summarizes the anecdotes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p440/r5.anchor: It is this motif which, in fact, is the summary of these anecdotes as well.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.claim: Through Aaron, the prophets are listed chronologically; afterward their order follows each prophet's attributes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p441/r1.anchor: Till the mention of Aaron (sws) all prophets are cited in the chronological order; after that the sequence is based on the attributes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r2.claim: The passengers decided to cast lots to identify the criminal aboard.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r2.anchor: At last, it was decided that lots will be cast to find out who that criminal was.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r4.claim: The passengers believed the ship could not escape the storm unless the apparent sinner was cast into the sea.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r4.anchor: sea the ship will not be able to come out of this storm.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r5.claim: The lots fell on Jonah, who was thrown into the sea.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p462/r5.anchor: The lots fell on Jonah (sws) and he was thrown into the sea.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r1.claim: The passengers may have chosen Jonah to cast lots because they regarded him as especially respectable, making his own selection ironic.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p463/r1.anchor: he would have been regarded as the most respectable and dignified person on the ship

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r4.claim: ‘Fled’ means ran away, ‘drew lots’ means cast lots, and ‘overturned’ means defeated or cast down.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p113#3/r4.anchor: أبق: هرب. ساهم: قارع. المدحض: المقلوب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud's report says the becalmed crew drew lots three times, Jonah's lot came up, and after seeing a sea creature await him at every side, he realized the event was from God and jumped to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود أنه لما أبعدت السفينة في البحر، ويونس فيها، ركدت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r7.claim: The defeated in the lots are literally those slipped away from the position of winning in the drawing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p123/r7.anchor: من المغلوبين، وحقيقته من المزلقين عن مقام الظفر في الاستفهام

SAMIN-DURR:37:141/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:37:141/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:37:141/r1.claim: ساهم means competing in drawing lots; originally the winning lot is the arrow that falls to the successful contestant.
SAMIN-DURR:37:141/r1.anchor: أي: فغالبهم في المساهمة، وهي الاقتراع. وأصله أن يخرج السهم على من غلب.

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n55/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n55/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n55/r1.claim: The phrase literally says Jonah cast lots with the mariner and was among the losers.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n55/r1.anchor: Lit., "he cast lots [with the mariner], and was among the losers".

ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n55/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n55/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n55/r2.claim: The Biblical account says Jonah admitted fleeing from God and asked to be thrown into the sea so the storm would calm; the sailors complied and the sea ceased raging.
ASAD-NOTES:37:139#n55/r2.anchor: According to the Biblical account (The Book of Jonah i, 10-l5), Jonah told them that he had "fled from the presence of the Lord"

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r1.claim: Jonah drew lots with the people aboard; this verse is evidence for those who hold that drawing lots is lawful.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r1.anchor: فقارع عليه السلام من في الفلك واستدل به من قال بمشروعية القرعة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r2.speaker: من قال بمشروعية القرعة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r2.claim: Jurists who cite the event take it as evidence that drawing lots is permitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r2.anchor: واستدل به من قال بمشروعية القرعة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r3.claim: Al-mudḥaḍīn means those defeated by the lot, literally people slipped from the station of victory.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r3.anchor: فصار من المغلوبين بالقرعة وأصله المزلق اسم مفعول عن مقام الظفر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r4.speaker: رُوي
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r4.claim: A report says Jonah announced punishment in three days, left before permission, and his people repented as it neared; ashamed to return after it was averted, he boarded a ship that stopped, and three lots selected him to be cast overboard.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p143#2/r4.anchor: يروى أنه وعد قومه العذاب وأخبرهم أنه يأتيهم إلى ثلاثة أيام فلما كان اليوم الثالث خرج يونس قبل أن يأذن الله تعالى له

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ووهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb say Jonah left after his people's punishment was delayed, boarded a ship, was identified as a runaway, lost three lots, then admitted it and jumped into the water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، ووهب: كان يونس وعد قومه العذاب، فلما تأخر عنهم العذاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r3.claim: Another story says waves separated Jonah from his wife and sons, a wolf took one son, and he boarded another ship that later stalled.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r3.anchor: وروي في القصة: أنه لما وصل إلى البحر كانت معه امرأته وابنان له، فجاء مركب فأراد أن يركب معهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r4.claim: Fasāhama means they cast lots; musāhama is casting arrows to draw a lot.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r4.anchor: فقارع، والمساهمة: إلقاء السهام على جهة القرعة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r5.claim: Al-mudḥaḍīn are those selected by lot.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p60/r5.anchor: {فساهم} فقارع، والمساهمة: إلقاء السهام على جهة القرعة، {فكان من المدحضين} المقروعين.

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r4.claim: They cast lots among the ship’s passengers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r4.anchor: فقارع أهله. { فكان من المدحضين } فصار من المغلوبين

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r5.claim: Jonah lost the drawing; the root image is slipping from a position of victory.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r5.anchor: فصار من المغلوبين بالقرعة، وأصله المزلق عن مقام الظفر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r6.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r6.claim: A report says Jonah left before God ordered him, boarded a ship that stopped, was identified as a fugitive, lost the lots, admitted fleeing, and threw himself into the water.
BAYDAWI-FULL:37:139-143/r6.anchor: روي أنه لما وعد قومه بالعذاب خرج من بينهم قبل أن يأمره الله

BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r10.speaker: البغوي
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r10.claim: Al-Baghawī explains musāhama as casting arrows to draw lots; Jonah cast lots with the crew, in keeping with their custom in such a crisis.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r10.anchor: قال البغوي : والمساهمة إلقاء السهام على جهة القرعة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r11.claim: The word evokes slipping on a slippery place: the lot made Jonah fall from his high position into the sea when the crew threw him overboard.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p340/r11.anchor: عبر عن ذلك بما يدل على الزلق الذي يكون من علو إلى سفل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.speaker: مترجمه
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.claim: The translator's Book of Jonah recounts Jonah's commission to Nineveh and flight by ship, a storm and lot that identify him, his being thrown overboard and swallowed by a great fish, and his prayer after three days and nights in its belly.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p343#2/r1.anchor: قال مترجمه : نبدأ بمعونة الله وقوته بكتب نبوة يونان بن متى النبي

DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.claim: When the boat stopped, its crew blamed an ill-omened passenger; lots fell to Jonah three times, and he jumped into the sea and was swallowed by the whale.
DURR-FULL:v7p120/r4.anchor: فلما لم يصبهم العذاب ذهب يونس عليه السلام مغاضبا فركب في البحر في سفينة مع أناس

DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.speaker: حميد بن هلال
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.claim: Hamid says the ship stalled, lots chose Jonah, and he asked to be tipped feet first into the sea; a pale-mouthed whale swallowed him, while a larger whale came after them.
DURR-FULL:v7p127/r5.anchor: فركب مع قوم في سفينة فجعلت السفينة لا تنفذ ولا ترجع فقال بعضهم لبعض ماذا إلا لذنب بعضكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r5.claim: Sāhama means to cast lots; the word derives from sahm, an arrow, since people drew lots using arrows called azlām.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r5.anchor: وأصله مشتق من اسم السهم لأنهم كانوا يقترعون بالسهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r6.claim: The consequence marker implies omitted events: the sea grew rough and the passengers feared drowning, so they cast lots; the author compares this ellipsis with Moses striking the sea and it splitting.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r7.speaker: كتاب يونان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r7.claim: The Jewish Book of Jonah says the passengers proposed casting lots to identify the cause of the calamity, and the lot fell on Jonah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r7.anchor: أن بعضهم قال لبعض : هلم نلقق قرعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ووهب بن منبه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Wahb ibn Munabbih report that the lot fell on Jonah three times.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس ووهب بن منبه أن القرعة خرجت ثلاث مرات على يونس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r9.claim: Ancient seafarers used lots when passengers or cargo overloaded a ship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r9.anchor: وسنة الاقتراع في أسفار البحر كانت متبعة عند الأقدمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r10.speaker: الصفدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r10.claim: Al-Ṣafadī recounts a sinking ship carrying Muslims and non-Muslims: instead of the dangerous direct lot, its leader counted people and threw every ninth person overboard until the non-Muslims were gone; his diagram marks Muslims in red and starts the count with them toward the north.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p173/r10.anchor: قصة الحيلة التي ذكرها الصفدي في

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.claim: The narrative omits intervening events for concision; Ibn ʿAṭiyya supplies a report that the ship stalled while other ships moved, so its crew blamed a sinner and cast lots.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r8.anchor: وهنا قصص محذوف إيجازا واختصارا، وروي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه لما حصل في السفينة وأبعدت في البحر ركدت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r9.claim: In Ibn Masʿūd's report, the sailors drew lots three times, each time naming Yūnus; when they resolved to throw him overboard, a sea creature watched him at every side of the ship, so he realized this was God's decree and leapt into its mouth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p485/r9.anchor: فطفا سهم يونس، ففعلوا نحو هذا ثلاث مرات في كل مرة تقع القرعة عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r1.claim: Sāhama means that they cast lots.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r2.claim: Al-mudḥaḍīn means those who were overcome.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r2.anchor: وساهم بمعنى قارع ﴿ من المدحضين ﴾ اي المغلوبين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r3.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains adḥaḍa as removing an argument so it slips away; the root sense of daḥḍ is slipperiness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة يقال أدحض الله حجته فدحضت أي أزالها فزالت وأصل الدحض الزلق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Jonah’s people repented after his three-day warning, so punishment was withheld; Jonah left angry, boarded a ship, said it carried a runaway servant, and lost the lots three times, though the crew initially refused to cast him out.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r5.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود لما وعد يونس قومه بالعذاب بعد ثلاث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r6.speaker: طاووس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r6.claim: Ṭāwūs gives another account: the ship’s captain called for lots because an ill-omened man prevented sailing, and Jonah lost three times.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p86#2/r6.anchor: قال طاووس إن صاحب السفينة هو الذي قال إنما يمنعها أن تسير أن فيكم رجلا مشؤوما فاقترعوا لنلقي أحدنا فاقترعوا فقرع يونس ثلاث مرات

BURSEVI:v7p379/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r3.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v7p379/r3.claim: The Imam reports sailors' view that a sinner was aboard, since the ship stopped without wind or apparent cause; merchants proposed drawing lots based on prior experience.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r3.anchor: وقال الإمام فقال الملاحون : إن فيكم عاصيا وإلا لم يحصل في السفينة ما نراه من غير ريح

BURSEVI:v7p379/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r4.claim: The merchants reasoned that sacrificing one was better than losing everyone; lots were drawn three times, and Jonah was selected each time.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r4.anchor: وقال التجار : قد جربنا مثل هذا فإذا رأينا نقترع فمن خرج سهمه نرميه في البحر

BURSEVI:v7p379/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r5.claim: The verb means Jonah joined the ship's people in drawing lots; a سهم is an arrow or similar object used for the draw.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r5.anchor: والمعنى فقارع أهل الفلك من الآبق وألقوا السهام على وجه القرعة.

BURSEVI:v7p379/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r6.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p379/r6.claim: Kashifi understands Jonah as the subject: Jonah cast lots with the ship's people three times.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r6.anchor: والمفهوم من تفسير الكاشفي أن الضمير إلى يونس يعني : (يونس قرعه زد باهل كشتى سه نوبت)

BURSEVI:v7p379/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p379/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p379/r7.claim: Those defeated by lot were overcome; the root evokes slipping away from victory, as a foot slips or an argument is invalidated.
BURSEVI:v7p379/r7.anchor: فصار من المغلوبين بالقرعة وأصله المزلق عن مقام الظفر والغلبة. قال في "القاموس" : دحضت رجله زلقت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.claim: Jonah's story was already recounted in Sura al-Anbiya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r1.anchor: قد تقدمت قصة يونس، عليه السلام، في سورة الأنبياء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r4.claim: Sahama means to draw lots, and al-mudhaddin means those who lost the lot.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r4.anchor: {فساهم} أي: قارع {فكان من المدحضين} أي: المغلوبين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r5.claim: As waves tossed the ship toward sinking, its crew drew lots for someone to be cast overboard and lighten it; Jonah lost three times, though they resisted, and he stripped to jump.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p38#2/r5.anchor: وذلك أن السفينة تلعبت (2) بها الأمواج من كل جانب، وأشرفوا على الغرق، فساهموا على من تقع عليه القرعة يلقى في البحر

JISHUMI:v8p5949/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r3.anchor: والمساهمة: إلقاء السهام على وجه القرعة

JISHUMI:v8p5949/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r4.claim: Daḥḍ is slipping or falling; the same root in “their argument is dāḥiḍah” means that it has fallen or failed.
JISHUMI:v8p5949/r4.anchor: والدحض: الزلق، دحض فهو داحض إذا سقط، ومنه: (حجتهم داحضة) أي: ساقطة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi say it means drawing lots with arrows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r10.anchor: أي قارع بالسهام , قاله ابن عباس والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r11.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say it means those defeated in the lot.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r11.anchor: أحدها : من المقروعين , قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r12.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says it means defeated; Abu Qays's verse supports this.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p66/r12.anchor: من المغلوبين , قاله سعيد بن جبير , ومنه قول أبي قيس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r1.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says it means a refuted argument, derived from argument invalidation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r1.anchor: أنه الباطل الحجة , قاله السدي مأخوذ من دحض الحجة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p67/r2.claim: After Jonah was thrown into the sea, the sailors believed.

MUJAHID:v2p545#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p545#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p545#3/r1.claim: Mujahid explains that Jonah was among those selected in the drawing of lots.
MUJAHID:v2p545#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فساهم فكان من المدحضين ﴾ يقول كان من المسهومين

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r5.claim: Jonah identified himself as the wanted man and asked to be thrown overboard; the crew refused because he was God’s messenger, then drew names in water three times, each time finding Jonah’s name, before casting him in.
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r5.anchor: قال: أنا المطلوب أنا يونس بن متى، فاقذفونى فى البحر

MUQATIL:37:137-140/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r6.claim: Before Jonah was thrown, God had not told the whale what to do; when Jonah was two spans from the water, God made its belly a place of worship and forbade it to harm his hair or skin or give him food or drink.
MUQATIL:37:137-140/r6.anchor: لى من عبدى حاجة إن لم أجعل عبدى لك رزقا، ولكن جعلت بطنك له مسجدا

MUQATIL:37:141-144/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r1.claim: Jonah drew lots and was the one defeated by the draw.
MUQATIL:37:141-144/r1.anchor: يعنى فقارعهم فكان من المقروعين المغلوبين

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#5/r1.claim: Jonah cast lots with them once or three times; musāhamah is casting arrows to draw lots.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#5/r1.anchor: فقارعهم مرة أو ثلاثا بالسهام والمساهمة إلقاء السهام على جهة القرعة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p28#5/r2.claim: He was among those defeated by the lot.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r7.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad glosses sāhama as drawing lots, from the arrows used in casting lots.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r7.anchor: قال المبرد: فقارع، قال: وأصله من السهام التي تجال

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r8.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r8.claim: Al-Mubarrad glosses al-mudḥaḍīn as the defeated.

QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r9.claim: Al-Farra links the word to slipping, as in a defeated argument; an anonymous poetic line uses al-mudḥaḍīn for the vanquished.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:140-144/r9.anchor: قال الفراء: دحضت حجته وأدحضها الله. وأصله من الزلق قال الشاعر

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet through Abu Hurayra says God ordered the whale to take Yunus without injuring flesh or breaking bone; Yunus heard sea creatures’ glorification, prayed, and was rescued after angels interceded, then was cast ashore sick.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r1.anchor: لما أراد الله تعالى ذكره حبس يونس في بطن الحوت أوحى الله إلى الحوت أن خذه

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r3.claim: A report cited by al-Zamakhshari says the whale swam beside the ship with Yunus breathing and praising from its raised head, then carried him to shore and expelled him unharmed.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r3.anchor: وقد روي: أن الحوت سار مع السفينة رافعا رأسه يتنفس فيه يونس ويسبح

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r4.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r4.claim: Ibn al-Arabi recounts that Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni was asked whether God is in a direction and answered no; he delayed his proof until a guest’s debt was paid, refusing to burden two volunteers when one could pay.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r4.anchor: وقال ابن العربي: أخبرني غير واحد من أصحابنا عن إمام الحرمين أبي المعالي عبد الملك

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r5.claim: The report cited as proof includes the Prophet’s statement, “Do not prefer me over Yunus ibn Matta.”
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r5.anchor: الدليل عليه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r6.speaker: إمام الحرمين الجويني
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r6.claim: Al-Juwayni argues that God is not spatially nearer to Muhammad in the ascent than to Yunus in the whale’s deepest sea darkness, supporting transcendence of direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r6.anchor: إمام الحرمين أبي المعالي عبد الملك بن عبد الله بن يوسف الجويني: أنه سئل عن الباري في جهة

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r7.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r7.claim: Al-Tabari reports that a violent storm led sailors to suspect one of them; Yunus confessed, asked to be cast overboard, lost the lots three times, and jumped into the sea at night, where the whale swallowed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r7.anchor: ذكر الطبري: أن يونس عليه السلام لما ركب في السفينة أصاب أهلها عاصف من الريح

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r8.claim: A second account says Yunus slept while covered; twice a storm nearly sank the ship, and after the sailors woke him to pray with them, his prayer was followed by the wind’s calming.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141/r8.anchor: وروي أنه لما ركب في السفينة تقنع ورقد فساروا غير بعيد إذ جاءتهم ريح

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r1.claim: In the continuation, the whale repeatedly surfaced by the ship; Yunus asked to be thrown over, lost repeated lots, then jumped into its mouth. God made its belly a container rather than food for him; after forty nights he prayed and was saved.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r1.anchor: فذلك قول الله عز وجل: { فساهم فكان من المدحضين } أي وقع السهم عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says drawing lots existed in earlier law and was also established in Islamic law, as discussed in Al Imran.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r2.anchor: ففي هذا من الفقه أن القرعة كانت معمولا بها في شرع من قبلنا، وجاءت في شرعنا

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi lists the Prophet drawing lots among his wives for travel, among six slaves when their owner had no other property, and directing litigants over an old inheritance to seek the truth and draw lots.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وقد وردت القرعة في الشرع في ثلاثة مواطن:

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r4.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r4.claim: These cases concern allocation among wives, manumission, and division of disputed property; lots remove ambiguity and prevent self-interested selection.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r4.anchor: فهذه ثلاثة مواطن، وهي القسم في النكاح، والعتق، والقسمة، وجريان القرعة فيها لرفع الإشكال

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r5.claim: Scholars differ over drawing lots among wives for a campaign, but the correct view, also held by jurists across the regions, is to draw lots because taking all is impossible and choosing one favors her.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r5.anchor: واختلف علماؤنا في القرعة بين الزوجات في الغزو على قولين الصحيح منهما الإقراع

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r6.claim: For the six slaves, two equaled the one-third limit for deathbed manumission; preference by whim was unlawful, leaving lots to select them.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r6.anchor: فإن كل اثنين منهما ثلث، وهو القدر الذي يجوز له فيه العتق في مرض الموت

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r7.claim: When parties dispute particular inherited objects, lots distinguish the right and appoint the recipient where the claim is unclear.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r7.anchor: وكذلك التشاجر إذا وقع في أعيان المواريث لم يميز الحق إلا القرعة

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Arabi’s own view is that lots should govern every ambiguous case because they most clearly resolve uncertainty and settle judgment.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r8.anchor: قال: والحق عندي أن تجري في كل مشكل، فذلك أبين لها، وأقوى لفصل الحكم فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r9.claim: On that principle, drawing lots among wives for divorce is analogous to drawing lots among enslaved women for manumission.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:141#2/r9.anchor: ولذلك قلنا: إن القرعة بين الزوجات في الطلاق كالقرعة بين الإماء في العتق

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r1.claim: Drawing lots to cast a person into the sea is forbidden; Yunus’s case was a unique preliminary to manifest proof and strengthen faith, not precedent for killing or throwing a sinner into fire or water.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r1.anchor: الاقتراع على إلقاء الآدمي في البحر لا يجوز

QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r2.claim: It is wrong to draw lots to choose passengers to throw overboard when a storm requires lightening the ship; the text says discarding men does not relieve it, and people should bear God’s decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:37:143-144/r2.anchor: فإنها لا تخف برمي بعض الرجال وإنما ذلك في الأموال

QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r7.claim: In the story, a whale waited at either side of the ship; Jonah understood the trial was meant for him, threw himself into the water, and it swallowed him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p303/r7.anchor: حتى جاز كل جانب . ثم لما علم أنه مراد بالبلاء ألقى نفسه في الماء فابتلعه الحوت

STUDYQURAN:37:140/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r1.speaker: the Biblical book of Jonah
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r1.claim: The Biblical account says Jonah fled God’s presence, a tempest struck the ship, sailors cast lots and identified him, and eventually threw him overboard, calming the sea.
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r1.anchor: According to the Biblical book of Jonah, Jonah, having fled “from the presence of the Lord”

STUDYQURAN:37:140/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r2.claim: IK reports that some Quranic commentators say the hesitant sailors watched Jonah throw himself into the fish’s mouth when it rose by God’s command.
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r2.anchor: the fish’s mouth when it rose, by God’s Command, to carry him away (IK)

STUDYQURAN:37:140/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r3.claim: Different accounts keep Jonah in the fish for three, seven, or forty days; another says he was swallowed in the morning and expelled that evening.
STUDYQURAN:37:140/r3.anchor: he was swallowed in the morning and cast out in the evening (IK)

TAB-FULL:v19p624/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r4.claim: “He drew lots” is al-Ṭabarī's explanation of Jonah's participation.

TAB-FULL:v19p624/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as drawing lots.

TAB-FULL:v19p624/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r6.claim: Qatāda says the ship stalled, the crew suspected a misdeed, cast lots, selected Jonah, and he threw himself overboard for the whale to swallow him.
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r6.anchor: قتادة، {فساهم فكان من المدحضين} [الصافات: 141] قال: «فاحتبست السفينة، فعلم القوم أنما احتبست من حدث أحدثوه، فتساهموا، فقرع يونس، فرمى بنفسه، فالتقمه الحوت»

TAB-FULL:v19p624/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r7.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v19p624/r7.claim: Al-Suddī also glosses the phrase as casting lots.

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r1.claim: Al-mudḥaḍīn are those overcome in the lot; the root image is slipping, and the idiom “God made his proof slip” means He invalidated it.
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r1.anchor: ابن عباس، قوله: {فكان من المدحضين} [الصافات: 141] يقول: «من المقروعين»

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r2.claim: The root's basic image is slipping in water or mud; the usage “dahḍa Allah his proof” is reported as uncommon.
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r2.anchor: ابن عباس، قوله: {فكان من المدحضين} [الصافات: 141] يقول: «من المقروعين»

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains them as those selected by lot.
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r3.anchor: ابن عباس، قوله: {فكان من المدحضين} [الصافات: 141] يقول: «من المقروعين»

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r4.claim: Mujāhid calls them those who drew lots.

TAB-FULL:v19p626/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r5.claim: Al-Suddī calls them those selected by lot.
TAB-FULL:v19p626/r5.anchor: السدي، قوله: {فكان من المدحضين} [الصافات: 141] قال: «من المقروعين»

TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.claim: Jonah boarded a laden ship; to save it, the crew cast lots for someone to throw to a great fish, Jonah was selected and cast into the sea, and the fish swallowed him as the ship escaped.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#2/r3.anchor: فساهموا وقارعوا فيما بينهم فأصابت يونس عليه السلام فألقوه في البحر فابتلعه الحوت ونجت السفينة

TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r1.speaker: الآلوسي
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r1.claim: In al-Ālūsī's biblical account, frightened sailors throw cargo overboard; Jonah sleeps below, the captain wakes him to pray, and the crew cast lots to identify the cause of the storm.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r1.anchor: ففزع الملاحون ورموا في البحر بعض الأمتعة لتخف السفينة

TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r2.speaker: الآلوسي
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r2.claim: The lot falls on Jonah; he identifies himself as servant of the Lord, maker of land and sea, and says to throw him overboard; the sailors try to reach shore, then cast him in and the sea calms.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#3/r2.anchor: فقال لهم أنا عبد الرب إله السماء خالق البر والبحر وأخبرهم خبره

TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r4.speaker: الصادق
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r4.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says that when people cast lots while entrusting their affair to God, the true lot emerges; no judgment is fairer than a God-entrusted lot.
TABATABAI:37:133-148#4/r4.anchor: وقال الصادق عليه السلام ما تقارع قوم ففوضوا أمرهم إلى الله عز وجل إلا خرج سهم الحق

TABRISI:37:137-141/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:137-141/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:137-141/r6.claim: Musahama is drawing lots, from casting arrows.
TABRISI:37:137-141/r6.anchor: والمساهمة المقارعة مأخوذ من إلقاء السهام

TABRISI:37:137-141/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:137-141/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:37:137-141/r7.claim: Dahadat means an argument failed; the root is slipping, since one who passes over a slippery place falls.
TABRISI:37:137-141/r7.anchor: ودحضت حجته أي سقطت وأدحضها الله مأخوذ من الدحض وهو الزلق

TABRISI:37:137-141/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:137-141/r8.speaker: شاعر
TABRISI:37:137-141/r8.claim: The quoted line “and he swerved as a camel swerves from a slippery place” illustrates dahd as a slippery surface; the poet is unnamed.
TABRISI:37:137-141/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: وحاد كما حاد البعير عن الدحض

TABRISI:37:137-141/r25.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:137-141/r25.speaker: الحسن، ابن عباس
TABRISI:37:137-141/r25.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn ʿAbbas say Jonah drew lots with the people and was among those who lost.
TABRISI:37:137-141/r25.anchor: أي من المقروعين عن الحسن وابن عباس

TABRISI:37:142-147/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:37:142-147/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the outcome as being among those selected by lot to be thrown into the sea.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r1.anchor: من المسهومين عن مجاهد والمراد من الملقين في البحر

TABRISI:37:142-147/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:37:142-147/r2.claim: One account says the ship faced sinking, so the people thought that throwing one passenger overboard would save the rest.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r2.anchor: واختلف في سبب ذلك فقيل: إنهم أشرفوا على الغرق فرأوا أنهم إن طرحوا واحدا منهم

TABRISI:37:142-147/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:37:142-147/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:37:142-147/r4.claim: A third account says the crew threw Jonah into the sea after the lot fell to him.
TABRISI:37:142-147/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنه لما وقعت القرعة عليه ألقوه في البحر

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r1.claim: Sāhama means that they cast lots.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r2.claim: Al-mudḥaḍīn are those who lost the casting of lots; the root's original sense is slipping, and to invalidate an argument makes it slip away.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r2.anchor: فكان من المدحضين} أي من المقروعين. يقال: أدحض الله حجته فدحضت؛ أي أزالها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r3.speaker: ابن عيينة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna explains sāhama as gambling and al-mudḥaḍīn as those who lost the gamble.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p374#4/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عيينة: {فساهم} أي قامر. {فكان من المدحضين} أي المقمورين"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r2.claim: Said b. Jubayr says the ship stalled mid-sea; Jonah confessed a grave sin and proposed a lot, which fell against him, so they cast him overboard.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r2.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جير: ركب يونس السفينة في البحر حتى إذا توسطت بهم ركدت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r3.speaker: وهب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r3.claim: Wahb says Jonah identified himself as the fugitive servant preventing the ship from moving; the lot selected him, and he threw himself into the sea.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r3.anchor: وقال وهب: لما احتبست السفينة قال: هاهنا عبد أبق من سيده، وهذا رسم السفينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r4.claim: The exegetes explain sāhama as drawing lots.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: {فساهم}: فقارع (¬6). قال المبرد: وإنما أخذ من السهام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r5.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives the word from the arrows used to draw lots.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p104#2/r5.anchor: قال المبرد: وإنما أخذ من السهام التي تحال للقرعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and the exegetes take al-mudḥaḍīn to mean the defeated, whose lot was overruled.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba relates the term to a proof being removed and to slipping, its root sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة. (يقال: أدحض الله حجته فدحضت، أي: أزالها فزالت)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r3.claim: Said b. Jubayr says a whale waited open-mouthed for its Lord's command and took Jonah when he was cast from the ship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v19p106/r3.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: لما استهموا في السفينة جاء حوت إلى السفينة فاغرا فاه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r2.claim: The ship stopped moving, so its passengers cast lots; Jonah lost, went out of the ship, and threw himself into the sea.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r2.anchor: فقارعه أهل السفينة فخرجت القرعة عليه، فخرج منها وألقى نفسه في البحر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r3.claim: Sāhama means to draw lots, and Jonah was among those defeated by the lot.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:37:140-148/r3.anchor: فقارع { فكان من المدحضين } المغلوبين بالقرعة

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r6.claim: When the ship would not move, its passengers suspected a wrongdoer aboard, cast lots, and Jonah was selected.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r6.anchor: فلما ركبها قامت فلم تسر، قال أهل السفينة: إن فيكم لمذنبا، قال: فتساهموا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r7.claim: Al-mudhahdin means those who lost the lot.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r7.anchor: فقرع يونس، وهو قوله: {فساهم فكان من المدحضين} [الصافات: 141] من المقروعين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r8.claim: Mujahid explains the word as those assigned a lot.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p841#2/r8.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المسهومين. فأوحى الله إلى الحوت

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r1.claim: The crew prayed through the wind and woke Jonah to pray with them; after the wind stopped and returned, he recognized that the trouble came from his own sin.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r1.anchor: ودعوا الله ثم قالوا: أيقظوا الرجل يدعو الله معنا، ففعلوا، فرفع الله عنهم تلك الريح،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r2.claim: Jonah asked the crew to bind and throw him into the sea, but they refused and proposed that the lot decide who should be cast overboard.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r2.anchor: فقال لأهل السفينة: شدوني وثاقا وألقوني في البحر فقالوا: ما كنا لنفعل

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r3.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r3.claim: Another account says Jonah wrapped himself in his cloak and tried to throw himself into the sea when the ship stalled, but the crew stopped him and chose lots.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: لما ركدت السفينة فلم تسر، لف نفسه في كسائه وأراد أن يطرح نفسه في البحر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r4.claim: The lot fell to Jonah three times; each time he said he had warned them, but the crew continued to draw lots until they selected him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r4.anchor: فأصابته القرعة فقال: قد أخبرتكم، فقالوا: ما كنا لنفعل، ولكن اقترعوا، فاقترعوا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r5.claim: The selected loser of the lot is one of the disqualified.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r5.anchor: وهو قول الله: {فساهم فكان من المدحضين} [الصافات: 141] ، أي: من المقروعين.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r6.claim: Mujahid says the lot was an arrow that landed on Jonah.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p842/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: من المسهومين، أي: وقع السهم عليه.

ELMALILI:37:139-179/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179/r3.claim: The translation says that lots were drawn and Yunus became one of those who lost.

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.claim: Alusi transmits the People of the Book's account: sent to Nineveh, overwhelmed by its wickedness, Yunus fled toward Tarshish via Jaffa and boarded a ship caught in a storm.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r3.anchor: Âlûsî tefsirinde der ki: “Yûnus aleyhisselâm hakkında ehl-i kitâbın kitaplarında mezkur olan şudur

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r4.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r4.claim: In that account, sailors cast lots to identify the cause of the storm; the lot fell to Yunus, who confessed his flight and told them to throw him overboard.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r4.anchor: gelin bu şer bize kimin sebebiyle geldi bilmek için kura atalım’ dediler, kura attılar Yûnus’a düştü.

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r5.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r5.claim: The sailors tried to return to shore, then threw Yunus in; the sea calmed, a great fish swallowed him, and he remained inside for three days and nights praying.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r5.anchor: nihâyet Yûnus’u tuttular, gemide bulunanların necâtı için denize attılar, derhâl deniz durdu

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r12.claim: Yunus fled to a fully laden ship; the sailors drew lots, and he was among those who lost and were cast out.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r12.anchor: Hani o dolu gemiye kaçmıştı {فَسَاهَمَ} da sehim, kura atışmıştı

ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r13.claim: Al-mudhaddin means those defeated in the lots and expelled from the ship; though some say Yunus threw himself, the wording's apparent sense does not support that, but he may have consented.
ELMALILI:37:139-179#2/r13.anchor: burada kendi kendini attı diye bir söz varsa da ٱلْمُدْحَضِينَ tâbirinin zâhirine muvâfık değildir

MAJAZ:v2p174/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p174/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p174/r4.claim: Arab usage has adḥaḍa ḥujjatahu for ‘he invalidated his argument’; al-daḥḍ is water or slippery ground, as in Dhu al-Iṣbaʿ’s ‘slippery, daḥḍ ground.’
MAJAZ:v2p174/r4.anchor: تقول العرب: أدحض الله حجته أي أبطلها والدحض الماء والزلق قال ذو الإصبع:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.claim: These verses briefly report what befell Jonah after he left his homeland; the Qur’an foregrounds the story’s instructive lesson rather than supplying bare history.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r6.anchor: Kur’an’ın amacı, salt tarihî bilgi vermek değil, olayın ibret verici yönünü öne çıkarmak olduğu için onun hayatı hakkında daha fazla ayrıntı vermeye gerek görülmemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.speaker: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.claim: The Bible’s fuller account broadly matches the Qur’an: sent to warn Nineveh, Jonah flees by ship toward Tarshish, is cast overboard by lot in a storm and swallowed; after prayer he is returned ashore, recommissioned, and Nineveh repents.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:37:139/r7.anchor: Kitâb-ı Mukaddes’te Hz. Yûnus hakkında genel hatlarıyla Kur’an’da verilenlerle de uyuşan daha ayrıntılı bilgi bulunmaktadır

NAHHAS:v3p438/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r8.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v3p438/r8.claim: Muhammad ibn Yazid glosses ساهم as drawing lots, originally referring to arrows cast for the lot.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r8.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد فقارع قال وأصله من السهام التي تجال

NAHHAS:v3p438/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p438/r9.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p438/r9.claim: Al-Farra explains المدحضين as those defeated by the lot; the root also describes an argument slipping.
NAHHAS:v3p438/r9.anchor: أي من المغلوبين به قال الفراء يقال دحضت حجته وأدحضها الله وأصله من الزلق

BURHAN:v1p106/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p106/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p106/r3.claim: دحض and داحض usually mean falsehood; المدحضين in al-Saffat is an exception with a different sense.

ITQAN:v2p417/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p417/r10.speaker: ابن فارس
ITQAN:v2p417/r10.claim: Ibn Faris says daḥḍ normally means falsehood, but al-mudḥaḍin means those defeated or overcome.
ITQAN:v2p417/r10.anchor: وكل ما فيه من الدحض فالباطل إلا ﴿ فكان من المدحضين ﴾ فمعناه من المقروعين
